summary.oneLiner: Vertically integrated cashew processor evolving into a diversified 'Food, Fuel, Feed and Fertility' agri-value platform under its long-term Strategy 2037 roadmap.
summary.business: Aelea Commodities Limited is a vertically integrated B2B and B2C agri-processing company that sources Raw Cashew Nuts from key African origins and Indian traders/MNCs and processes them into premium-quality cashew kernels and branded consumer products for domestic and international customers. Under Strategy 2037 the Company is progressing towards backward integration, by-product valorisation (CNSL, Cardanol, activated carbon, bio-charcoal) and renewable energy initiatives to build a circular, diversified agri-value enterprise.

risks.risk: Volatility in Raw Cashew Nut (RCN) prices
risks.note: RCN is the Company's core input, sourced from African origins and Indian traders/MNCs; price swings directly affect processing margins and working capital needs.
The business depends on cross-border shipment of RCN from African origins and export of finished kernels/products, exposing it to shipping and supply-chain bottlenecks.
Import of RCN and export sales, plus a foreign (UAE, AED-denominated) subsidiary, expose the Company to currency movements.
Flagged by management as a major risk in a global cashew processing industry with many established domestic and international processors.
Climatic uncertainty affecting RCN crop yields and availability is explicitly flagged as a risk to raw-material supply.
Export markets and institutional/branded customers require consistent compliance with food-safety and quality standards; a lapse could affect customer relationships and export readiness.
A commodity-processing, import/export-heavy model is working-capital intensive; management specifically flags working capital requirements as a major risk area.

risks.risk: Technology adoption and project execution risk on downstream integration
risks.note: Future by-product/renewable-energy projects (CNSL, Cardanol, Unit III, etc.) under Strategy 2037 carry execution and technology-adoption risk as the Company moves beyond core kernel processing.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aelea Commodities Limited is a vertically integrated B2B and B2C agri-processing company that sources Raw Cashew Nuts from key African origins and Indian traders/MNCs and processes them into premium-quality cashew kernels and branded consumer products for domestic and international customers. Under Strategy 2037 the Company is progressing towards backward integration, by-product valorisation (CNSL, Cardanol, activated carbon, bio-charcoal) and renewable energy initiatives to build a circular, diversified agri-value enterprise.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: similar high growth trajectory as FY26 (112%); margin: EBITDA margin target ~10-11% industry norm; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: Phase 2 CNSL plant commissioning expected H2FY27; Phase 3 capex to follow post-phase 2 stabilization

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into almond, walnut, pistachio, makhana processing by 2037; 100 premium retail stores via franchise model; entry into rice, sugar, wheat value-added processing with Africa export focus; CNSL oil scaling to industrial-grade biofuel and green thermal applications

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue growth supported by improved processing throughput, stronger customer demand, efficient procurement practices, and expansion across domestic as well as international markets
- Management expects value-added processing, integrated resource utilisation and diversified product offerings to gradually strengthen operating margins and resource productivity as the Company progresses on the Strategy 2037 roadmap
- Global cashew kernel demand currently in the range of 1.2-1.3 million tons, broadly in line with available supply; India is the largest consumer (~30% of global demand), followed by the European Union (~25%), United States (~11-12%), China (~8-10%) and Middle East (~7%)
- Industry increasingly exploring commercial utilisation of cashew by-products (CNSL, biofuels, industrial oils, activated carbon, biochar, renewable energy, animal nutrition products), creating opportunities for integrated processors capable of building diversified value chains
- Indian cashew demand supported by urbanisation, rising disposable income, growing health awareness, expansion of organised/modern retail, and a supportive government policy environment for food processing, value addition and exports
- Continued expansion of customer relationships across institutional and retail segments and continued development of branded retail products

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 11.07% (FY26) from prior levels due to scale and value-added byproducts; finance cost rose to Rs 8 Cr (from Rs 2 Cr in H1) due to direct farm-gate sourcing from Africa — higher input cost but better margins; CNSL oil contributes ~10% EBITDA margin at product level

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing debt-funded capex for value chain integration (CNSL, biochar); no equity dilution planned; focus on self-sustaining cash flow via back-to-back trading model; retail expansion via franchise (low capex)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aelea scaled up its Surat Unit-II processing line during FY26, expanding installed capacity from 40 MTPD to 140 MTPD, with facilities spread across approximately 2,38,454 sq. ft. The Company has secured 2,38,454 sq. ft. of additional land for future expansion and, during FY26, completed land acquisition and laid the foundation for Unit III, which is planned to focus on Cardanol, Bio Charcoal and De-oil Cake production as part of its multi-phase backward-integration and by-product-valorization strategy (CNSL processing, Cardanol production, Activated Carbon, Bio-charcoal and other value-added applications). Under Phase I of its roadmap the Company intends to continue expanding processing capacity, improve operational efficiencies, strengthen procurement (local and global farm-gate sourcing) and increase automation. The Company also obtained additional term loans/working capital facilities during the year to fund this expansion.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, visionary, and disciplined; management emphasizes long-term (2037) strategy over short-term guidance; transparent about aggressive value chain deepening; acknowledges finance cost increase as strategic, not a flaw; tone is founder-led with ESG and sustainability as core pillars

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated B2B and B2C model spanning procurement, processing, grading, packaging, distribution, branding and value addition
- Diversified raw-material sourcing: direct procurement from key African origins plus reputed Indian traders and MNCs, using pre-shipment, port-level and spot purchase models
- Automation-led production and quality assurance systems at an FSSC 22000-certified manufacturing facility
- Growing branded retail presence under 'Tryble & Supreme Cashew' across retail and e-commerce channels
- Strategy 2037 diversification into cashew by-product valorisation (CNSL, Cardanol, activated carbon, bio-charcoal) creating additional revenue pools beyond kernel processing

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Supply chain volatility from Africa (logistics delays); regulatory delays in solar approvals; CNSL market price volatility; execution risk in scaling 10 new commodities by 2037; B2C brand building requires long-term investment

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: CNSL oil is not just a byproduct — it's a high-margin, ESG-certified industrial fuel with premium pricing potential tied to ISCC EU certification; the 95% Africa sourcing is indirect via Singapore/Dubai traders, not direct farm-gate yet — a key future lever; B2C is intentionally minimal (1%) to avoid e-commerce burn, favoring franchise model for sustainable margins

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strategy 2037: long-term roadmap to transform Aelea into an integrated 'Food, Fuel, Feed and Fertility' enterprise, diversifying beyond kernel processing into value-added food products, renewable energy, industrial applications, animal nutrition and sustainable agricultural inputs
- Continued vertical integration across procurement, processing, grading, packaging, distribution, branding and value addition to improve control over quality, margins and customer experience
- Growth via two new wholly-owned subsidiaries — Aelea Green Energy Limited (renewable energy, biofuel, sustainable solutions) …
